<P ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="de1746_part_i_#151;financial_information"> </A>
<A NAME="toc_de1746_1"> </A>
<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B>PART I&#151;FINANCIAL INFORMATION    <BR>  </B></FONT></P>


<P><FONT SIZE=2><B>Background Information about the Company  </B></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We design, build, and market single-family attached and detached homes to entry-level and first-time move-up buyers and, to a lesser
extent, second-time move-up buyers in major suburban markets in California, Colorado, Hawaii, Washington, Oregon and Arizona. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
were formed in order to effect the combination of the operations of Western Pacific and Schuler Residential,&nbsp;Inc. (formerly Schuler Homes,&nbsp;Inc.). On April&nbsp;3,
2001, the operations of the two entities were combined. On June&nbsp;21, 2001, we effectuated the upstream merger of Schuler Residential into ourselves. </FONT></P>


<P><FONT SIZE=2><I>Schuler Residential  </I></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our co-Chairman, President and CEO, James K. Schuler, originally began business in the Hawaii market in 1973. In 1992, the former Schuler
Homes,&nbsp;Inc., which changed its name to Schuler Residential,&nbsp;Inc., became our subsidiary on April&nbsp;2, 2001 and was subsequently merged into us on June&nbsp;21, 2001, completed its
initial public offering and in late 1996 adopted a strategic expansion plan designed to geographically diversify its operations outside of the Hawaii market. As part of its diversification strategy,
the California, Colorado, Washington, Oregon and Arizona housing markets were entered either by acquiring existing homebuilders or starting new homebuilding divisions. </FONT></P>


<P><FONT SIZE=2><I>Western Pacific  </I></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Western Pacific was formed in December&nbsp;1993 by Eugene S. Rosenfeld, our co-Chairman, with the objective of taking advantage of the
anticipated recovery of the residential real estate market in California. Mr.&nbsp;Rosenfeld began his career in homebuilding in 1963 at Kaufman&nbsp;&amp; Broad,&nbsp;Inc., later serving as its CEO
from 1968 to 1976. Western Pacific began operations in Orange County and the Inland Empire in 1993 and expanded its presence in southern California by entering San Diego County in 1995, Los Angeles
County in 1996 and Ventura County in 1997. In order to achieve geographic
diversification outside Southern California, Western Pacific began operations in northern California in 1996 in the South Bay area of San Francisco and entered San Jose in 1997. </FONT></P>


<P><FONT SIZE=2><I>The Merger  </I></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On April&nbsp;3, 2001, the operations of Western Pacific and Schuler Residential,&nbsp;Inc. (formerly Schuler Homes,&nbsp;Inc.) were combined, and on
June&nbsp;21, 2001, we effectuated the upstream merger of Schuler Residential into ourselves. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><I>2001 Notes Offering  </I></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On June&nbsp;28, 2001, we consummated the issuance and sale of our 9<SUP>3</SUP>/<SMALL>8</SMALL>% Senior Notes due 2009, in the aggregate principal amount of
$250&nbsp;million and of our 10<SUP>1</SUP>/<SMALL>2</SMALL>% Senior Subordinated Notes due 2011, in the aggregate principal amount of $150&nbsp;million (collectively, the "Notes"). The proceeds of the
offering of the Notes were used to repay a substantial portion of our and our subsidiaries' outstanding indebtedness (other than our 9% Senior Notes due 2008). </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><I>New Banking Revolving Credit Facility  </I></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In conjunction with the offerings of the Notes, we also closed a $225&nbsp;million senior unsecured revolving credit facility with Bank of America, N.A.,
Fleet National Bank, First Hawaiian Bank and California Bank&nbsp;&amp; Trust. Subject to the satisfactory completion of further syndication efforts, we have the ability increase the amount of the
Revolving Credit Facility to an amount not exceeding $400&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT SIZE=2>3</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<!-- ZEQ.=1,SEQ=3,EFW="2055720",CP="SCHULER HOMES, INC.",DN="1",CHK=353445,FOLIO='3',FILE='DISK012:[01MOC6.01MOC1746]DE1746A.;9',USER='JHILL',CD='13-AUG-2001;16:21' -->
<A NAME="page_de1746_1_4"> </A>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><I>Financial Information included in this Form&nbsp;10-Q  </I></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The financial information in this Form&nbsp;10-Q for the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2001 is consolidated as a result of the merger. However,
the comparison to prior periods is shown in two different ways. In "Item 1. Financial Statements", the prior period presented includes the predecessor only, as required by accounting principles
generally accepted in the United States. In "Item 2. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations", the prior period is shown on a pro forma combined basis to
give effect to the merger as if it had occurred on April&nbsp;1, 2000. Accordingly,
the discussion of the results of operations in Item 2 is based on a comparison of the results for the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2001 to pro forma combined results for the quarter ended
June&nbsp;30, 2000. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT SIZE=2>4</FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><A

<A NAME="toc_fb1746_1"> </A>
<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B>Item 1. Financial Statements    <BR>  </B></FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT SIZE=2><B>INDEPENDENT ACCOUNTANTS' REVIEW REPORT  </B></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>The
Board of Directors and Stockholders<BR>
Schuler Homes,&nbsp;Inc. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
have reviewed the accompanying interim consolidated balance sheet of Schuler Homes,&nbsp;Inc. as of June&nbsp;30, 2001, and the related consolidated statements of income for
the three-month periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2001 and 2000, the consolidated statement of stockholders' equity for the three-month period ended June&nbsp;30, 2001, and the consolidated statements
of cash flows for the three-month periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2001 and 2000. These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company's management. </FONT></P>


<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
conducted our reviews in accordance with standards established by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants. A review of interim financial information consists
principally of applying analytical procedures to financial data, and making inquiries of persons responsible for financial and accounting matters. It is substantially less in scope than an audit
conducted in accordance with auditing standards generally accepted in the United States, which will be performed for the full year with the objective of expressing an opinion regarding the financial
statements taken as a whole. Accordingly, we do not express such an opinion. </FONT></P>


<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Based
on our reviews, we are not aware of any material modifications that should be made to the accompanying interim consolidated financial statements referred to above for them to be
in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
have previously audited, in accordance with auditing standards generally accepted in the United States, the consolidated balance sheet of Schuler Residential,&nbsp;Inc. (formerly
Schuler Homes,&nbsp;Inc.) as of March&nbsp;31, 2001, and the related consolidated statements of income, stockholders' equity, and cash flows for the year then ended (not presented herein) and in
our report dated May&nbsp;16, 2001, we expressed an unqualified opinion on those consolidated financial statements. In our opinion, the information set forth in the accompanying consolidated balance
sheet as of March&nbsp;31, 2001, is fairly stated, in all material respects, in relation to the consolidated balance sheet from which it has been derived. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><B>1.&nbsp;&nbsp;General  </B></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The accompanying unaudited consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United
States for interim financial information and with the instructions to Form&nbsp;10-Q and Article&nbsp;10 of Regulation&nbsp;S-X. Accordingly, they do not include all of
the information and footnotes required by accounting principles generally accepted in the United States for complete financial statements. In the opinion of management, all adjustments (consisting of
normal recurring adjustments) considered necessary for a fair presentation have been included. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;These
interim financial statements should be read in conjunction with the financial statements of Schuler Residential,&nbsp;Inc. (previously Schuler Homes,&nbsp;Inc.) and Western
Pacific contained in the Company's March&nbsp;31, 2001 annual report on Form&nbsp;10-K. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Company has experienced, and expects to continue to experience, significant variability in quarterly sales and net income. The results of any interim period are not necessarily
indicative of the results that can be expected for the entire year. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
preparation of financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States requires management to make estimates and assumptions that
affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses
during the reporting period. Actual results could differ from those estimates. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain
amounts in the prior period's financial statements have been reclassified to conform with the financial statement presentations in the current period. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
June&nbsp;2001, the Financial Accounting Standards Board issued Statements No.&nbsp;141, "Business Combinations", and No.&nbsp;142, "Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets",
effective for fiscal years beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2001. Under the new rules, goodwill and intangible assets deemed to have indefinite lives will no longer be amortized but will be subject
to annual impairment tests in accordance with the Statements. Other intangible assets will continue to be amortized over their useful lives. The Company has early-adopted the new rules on accounting
for goodwill and other intangible assets beginning April&nbsp;1, 2001. As a result, the Company has allocated its goodwill to its single homebuilding reporting unit and performed the required
goodwill impairment test. During the three months ended June&nbsp;30, 2001, the Company has not recognized any impairment losses related to its goodwill. Application of the nonamortization
provisions of the Statement has resulted in a reduction in amortization expense of approximately $1,374 for the three months ended June&nbsp;30, 2001 compared to the results had the Statement not
been adopted. The following summarizes the pro forma impact of the </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><B>2.&nbsp;&nbsp;Merger with Western Pacific  </B></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On September&nbsp;12, 2000, Schuler Residential,&nbsp;Inc. (previously Schuler Homes,&nbsp;Inc., "Schuler Residential") and the owners of Western Pacific
Housing ("Western Pacific") entered into an agreement and plan of merger in which the parties agreed to combine their separate businesses. Schuler Homes,&nbsp;Inc., a Delaware corporation
(previously Schuler Holdings,&nbsp;Inc., the "Company") was formed on October&nbsp;12, 2000. The Company was formed to own the businesses of Schuler Residential and under the merger, which
occurred on April&nbsp;2, 2001, the Schuler Residential stockholders received one share of Class&nbsp;A common stock of the Company for each share of Schuler Residential common stock they held. As
a result of the merger, Schuler Residential became a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company and the Company changed its name to Schuler Homes,&nbsp;Inc. In connection with the merger, the Company
acquired all of the ownership interests in Western Pacific, effectively combining the operations of Schuler Residential and Western Pacific. The Company issued to the owners of Western Pacific and to
one of its lenders an aggregate number of shares of the Company's Class&nbsp;B common stock equal to the number of shares of the Company's Class&nbsp;A common stock issued to Schuler </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT SIZE=2>11</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<!-- ZEQ.=2,SEQ=11,EFW="2055720",CP="SCHULER HOMES, INC.",DN="1",CHK=246400,FOLIO='11',FILE='DISK012:[01MOC6.01MOC1746]FK1746A.;14',USER='JHILL',CD='14-AUG-2001;14:56' -->
<A NAME="page_fk1746_1_12"> </A>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>
Residential stockholders as a result of the merger. On June&nbsp;21, 2001, Schuler Residential merged into the Company. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As
a result of the transactions described above, the historical results of Western Pacific are not reflected in those of the Company prior to April&nbsp;3, 2001. As such, the
accompanying consolidated financial statements reflect the historical results of Schuler Residential (the predecessor entity) as of March&nbsp;31, 2001 and for the three-month period ended
June&nbsp;30, 2000 and the historical results of the Company (including the combined businesses of Schuler Residential and Western Pacific) as of June&nbsp;30, 2001 and for the three-month period
ended June&nbsp;30, 2001. See Note&nbsp;9 for pro forma condensed combined financial data for the three-month period ended June&nbsp;30, 2000 giving effect to the transactions described above as
if they had occurred on April&nbsp;1, 2000. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
merger of Schuler Residential with the Company is accounted for on a historical cost basis, with the historical results of Schuler Residential prior to the merger presented as
those of the Company. The contribution of Western Pacific to the Company is treated as a "purchase" by the Company of Western Pacific for accounting purposes. Under this method, the Western Pacific
assets acquired and liabilities assumed were recorded on the Company's balance sheet at their fair market value as of April&nbsp;3, 2001 based on the following: </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
actual number of shares of Class&nbsp;B common stock issued in connection with the merger equaled the number of shares of Schuler Residential common stock outstanding at the
consummation of the merger. The estimated fair market value per share of the Class&nbsp;B common stock reflected a nominal discount to the average market price of the Schuler Residential common
stock for several days before and after the announcement of the merger on September&nbsp;12, 2001. The nominal discount is based on the different terms of the Class&nbsp;A and Class&nbsp;B
common stock, as well as the trading restrictions on the Class&nbsp;B common stock. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
connection with the merger with Western Pacific, the Company purchased minority interests for $9,000, which is payable as follows: $2,500 upon completion of the merger (paid in
April&nbsp;2001), $2,000 on the one-year anniversary of the completion of the merger, and a note for $4,500 that matures four years after the completion of the merger and that bears
interest at 7%. The note payable can be offset against a related note receivable in other assets and, as a result, the Company has a net liability of $2,000, which is reflected in accounts payable and
accrued liabilities at June&nbsp;30, 2001. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
deferred income tax liability is related to the income tax effect of timing differences created as a result of the contribution to the Company of the ownership interests in
Western Pacific that were previously held in limited partnerships and limited liability companies. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On
June&nbsp;28, 2001, the Company obtained a new senior unsecured revolving credit facility from a consortium of banks in the amount of $225,000 (the "Revolving Credit Facility")
for general corporate and working capital purposes. Subject to the satisfactory completion of further syndication efforts, the Company has the ability to increase the amount of the Revolving Credit
Facility to an amount not exceeding $400,000. Up to $50,000 of the Revolving Credit Facility may be used for letters of credit. Amounts available under the Revolving Credit Facility are subject to
certain borrowing base limitations based upon, among other things, the amount of certain outstanding debt and the amount of the Company's eligible inventory, multiplied by advance rates determined by
reference to the stage of development of each item of eligible inventory. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Company may select an interest rate applicable to the borrowings under the Revolving Credit Facility based on either LIBOR, for a one, two, three or six-month term, or
the prime rate. Subject to the Company's then-effective leverage ratio, as defined, the interest rate may vary from LIBOR plus 1.75% to 2.50% or the prime rate plus 0% to 0.50%. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Revolving Credit Facility is guaranteed by certain of our wholly-owned subsidiaries. It has a three-year term, extendible out to a full three-year term on
each anniversary of the closing date at the banks' discretion. Under the terms of the Revolving Credit Facility, the Company will be required to meet certain covenants and financial tests on an
on-going basis. As of June&nbsp;30, 2001, the Company met such covenants and financial tests. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;At
June&nbsp;30, 2001, there were no outstanding borrowings under the Revolving Credit Facility. At that date, the Company's maximum limit for borrowings and additional financial
letters of credit was $176,327 pursuant to the Company's borrowing base limit. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><B>5.&nbsp;&nbsp;Commitments and Contingencies  </B></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Commitments and contingencies consist of those normal and usual to real estate developers and include such items as land purchase contracts, subdivision
improvement agreements and guarantees, bond guarantees and warranties to homebuyers. In addition, the Company has continuing litigation matters incurred in the ordinary course of business and records
the liability for those contingencies when such amounts can be estimated and are considered to be material to the results of operations. Management believes that the disposition of the various matters
will not have a material effect on the consolidated financial position or operations of the Company. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><B>6.&nbsp;&nbsp;Income Taxes  </B></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During the three months ended June&nbsp;30, 2001 and 2000, the Company made income tax payments, net of refunds, of $6,439 and $12,600 respectively. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><B>7.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net Income Per Share  </B></FONT></P>


<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Basic net income per share for the three-month periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2001 and 2000 were computed using the weighted average number of common shares
outstanding during the periods of 40,436,247 and 20,100,946, respectively. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Diluted
net income per share for the three-month periods ended June&nbsp;30, 2001 and 2000 were computed by adding to net income the interest expense of $570 and $720, respectively
(net of related income taxes), which is applicable to convertible subordinated debentures, and dividing by 43,680,179 and 22,734,936, respectively, which represents the weighted average number of
shares assuming conversion of all convertible subordinated debentures and the exercise under the treasury stock method of all in-the-money stock options outstanding. </FONT></P>

their admittance as partners to a limited partner of one of the Company's stockholders. The loans are secured by the individuals' partnership </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="fm1746_item_2._management_s_discussio__ite03663"> </A>
<A NAME="toc_fm1746_1"> </A>
<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B>Item 2. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations    <BR>  </B></FONT></P>


<P><FONT SIZE=2><B>Overview  </B></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We design, build and market single-family attached and detached homes to entry-level and first-time move-up buyers and, to a lesser
extent, second-time move-up buyers in major suburban markets in Northern California, Southern California, Colorado, Hawaii, Washington, Oregon and Arizona. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
were formed in connection with the April&nbsp;3, 2001 merger in which the businesses of Western Pacific Housing and Schuler Residential,&nbsp;Inc. (formerly Schuler
Homes,&nbsp;Inc.) were combined. As our combined operating history began at that time, comparisons to our financial condition and results of operations at and for the quarter ended June&nbsp;30,
2000 described in this section are based upon the pro forma combined historical operations of Schuler Residential and Western Pacific at and for the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2000. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
recorded revenues of $315.2&nbsp;million, primarily from the closings of 1,164 new homes during the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2001, a 29.1% increase as compared to pro forma
combined revenues of $244.2&nbsp;million, primarily from the pro forma combined closings of 1,057 new homes during the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2000. Net income during the quarter ended
June&nbsp;30, 2001 totaled $16.9&nbsp;million (with diluted earnings of $0.40 per share), a 37.4% increase from pro forma combined net income of $12.3&nbsp;million ($0.30 diluted earnings per
share) during the same quarter in 2000. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;At
June&nbsp;30, 2001, we had 1,970 sales in backlog with an aggregate dollar value of $550.0&nbsp;million, 79 active projects in the sales stage, and control of over 28,500 lots,
approximately 50% of which are under option. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On
June&nbsp;28, 2001, we consummated the issuance and sale of our 9<SUP>3</SUP>/<SMALL>8</SMALL>% Senior Notes due 2009, in the aggregate principal amount of $250&nbsp;million and our
10<SUP>1</SUP>/<SMALL>2</SMALL>% Senior Subordinated Notes due 2011, in the aggregate principal amount of $150&nbsp;million (collectively, the "Notes"). </FONT></P>


<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
conjunction with the offerings of the Notes, we also closed a $225&nbsp;million senior unsecured revolving credit facility with Bank of America, N.A., Fleet National Bank, First
Hawaiian Bank and California Bank&nbsp;&amp; Trust. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><B>Results of Operations  </B></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The financial statements included herein in "PART I. Item 1. Financial Statements" include comparisons to predecessor-only financial statements at
and for the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2000, as required by accounting principles generally accepted in the United States. In order to provide a more meaningful comparison, included below is
statements of income data, which includes a comparison to unaudited proforma combined statement of income data that give effect to the merger as if it had occurred on April&nbsp;1, 2000. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;While
this pro forma information is based on adjustments deemed appropriate and which are factually supported based on currently available data, the pro forma information may not be
indicative of what actual results would have been, nor does this information purport to present financial results for future periods. </FONT></P>

<DT><FONT SIZE=2>(1)</FONT></DT><DD><FONT SIZE=2>Includes

the total number of projects owned or under option or similar contract, including projects with homes in the sales stage, under construction and projects in various stages
of planning.

the number of active projects in respect of which home or lot sales closed or homebuyers have entered into standard sales contracts and there remain at least seven unsold
homes in the project.
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT><FONT SIZE=2>(4)</FONT></DT><DD><FONT SIZE=2>Represents
the estimated number of homes based on approximately 14,300 lots relating to land owned and approximately 14,200 lots relating to land under option or similar contracts,
including homes under construction and backlog. Although we currently intend to consummate the purchase of the parcels under purchase options or similar contracts, we cannot assure you that we will
complete the purchases or acquire the land purchase option. </FONT></DD></DL>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><I>New Home Orders and Backlog  </I></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New home orders during the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2001 totaled 1,409, a 16.7% increase as compared to pro forma combined new home orders of 1,207 during
the same quarter in 2000. This was accomplished with only an 8.6% increase in the number of active projects in the sales stage. The increase in new home orders reflects the strength in our California
markets, especially in Southern California, where we have increased our focus on first-time buyers. As a result of our increased presence in the first-time buyer segment in
Southern California, we have decreased the average sales price per new home order in that area from $341,000 during the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2000 on a pro forma combined basis to $295,000
during the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2001. </FONT></P>


<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
aggregate sales value of homes in backlog at June&nbsp;30, 2001 increased by 20.7% from a year ago, reflecting an 18.0% increase in the number of homes in backlog and a 2.2%
increase in the average sales price of homes in backlog. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT SIZE=2>19</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<!-- ZEQ.=1,SEQ=19,EFW="2055720",CP="SCHULER HOMES, INC.",DN="1",CHK=924807,FOLIO='19',FILE='DISK012:[01MOC6.01MOC1746]FO1746A.;8',USER='CBABB',CD='14-AUG-2001;12:04' -->
<A NAME="page_fo1746_1_20"> </A>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><I>Revenues  </I></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We recorded revenues of $315.2&nbsp;million during the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2001, or 29.1% increase as compared to pro forma combined revenues of
$244.2&nbsp;million during the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2000. This is a result of a 15.3% increase in the number of homes closed and a 10.8% increase in the average sales price of homes closed,
reflecting a larger portion of homes closed in California and a
smaller portion of homes closed in Colorado in the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2001 as compared to the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2000 on a pro forma combined basis. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><I>Cost of Sales  </I></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Cost of sales as a percentage of revenues increased slightly from 78.5% during the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2000 on a pro forma combined basis to 79.1%
during the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2001, primarily reflecting a differing product mix between the periods. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><I>Selling, General and Administrative Expense  </I></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our selling, general and administrative expense decreased slightly from 11.9% during the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2000 on a pro forma combined basis to
11.7% during the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2001. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><I>Interest and Other Income (Expense)  </I></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest and other income (expense) decreased by $2.7&nbsp;million from the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2000 on a pro forma combined basis to the quarter
ended June&nbsp;30, 2001. This was primarily due to a)&nbsp;amortization of intangibles and forgiveness of a portion of a note receivable during the June&nbsp;30, 2000 quarter relating to the
departure of the former president of our Oregon division and b)&nbsp;increased marketing fees earned during the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2001 relating to the sale of model homes previously
under leaseback. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><I>Minority Interest in Income of Consolidated Joint Ventures  </I></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Minority interest in income of consolidated joint ventures remained consistent at $0.8&nbsp;million and $0.9&nbsp;million during the quarters ended
June&nbsp;30, 2001 and 2000, respectively. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><I>Provision for Income Taxes  </I></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our effective income tax rate was 39.9% and 38.5% for the quarters ended June&nbsp;30, 2001 and 2000, respectively. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2><B>Liquidity and Capital Resources  </B></FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We require significant capital resources to acquire land, develop land into building lots, construct and market our homes and pay our overhead and
administrative expenses. In addition, funds are required for market expansion and to make interest and principal payments on outstanding debt. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On
June&nbsp;28, 2001, we consummated the issuance and sale of our 9<SUP>3</SUP>/<SMALL>8</SMALL>% Senior Notes due 2009, in the aggregate principal amount of $250&nbsp;million and our
10<SUP>1</SUP>/<SMALL>2</SMALL>% Senior Subordinated Notes due 2011, in the aggregate principal amount of $150&nbsp;million (collectively, the "Notes"). In connection with the issuance and sale of the Notes,
we entered into (i)&nbsp;a Purchase Agreement with the Company's subsidiaries, and with UBS Warburg LLC, Banc of America Securities LLC, Fleet Securities,&nbsp;Inc. and Salomon Smith
Barney&nbsp;Inc. (collectively, the "Initial Purchasers") providing for the purchase of the Notes by the Initial Purchasers; (ii)&nbsp;Registration Rights Agreements with the Company's
subsidiaries and the Initial Purchasers, pursuant to which we agreed to file&nbsp;a registration statement within 90&nbsp;days with the Securities and Exchange Commission with respect to the offer
and sale of $400&nbsp;million in aggregate principal amount of notes (the "Exchange Notes") that will be issued and offered in </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT SIZE=2>20</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<!-- ZEQ.=2,SEQ=20,EFW="2055720",CP="SCHULER HOMES, INC.",DN="1",CHK=858224,FOLIO='20',FILE='DISK012:[01MOC6.01MOC1746]FO1746A.;8',USER='CBABB',CD='14-AUG-2001;12:04' -->
<A NAME="page_fo1746_1_21"> </A>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>
exchange for the Notes in an exchange offer, as well as to register the Notes pursuant to one or more shelf registrations under certain circumstances, all at our expense; and (iii)&nbsp;Indentures
with U.S. Bank Trust National Association, as Trustee, pursuant to which the Notes and the Exchange Notes will be governed. The Company will file a Form S-4 Registration Statement with the U.S.
Securities and Exchange Commission to register the Exchange Notes. The Company received net proceeds from the offering of approximately $391,200. We repaid a substantial portion of our and our
subsidiaries' outstanding indebtedness (other than our 9% Senior Notes due 2008 and the convertible debentures due January&nbsp;2003) with the proceeds of the offering of the Notes. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
conjunction with the offerings of the Notes, we also closed a transaction with Bank of America, N.A., Fleet National Bank, First Hawaiian Bank and California Bank&nbsp;&amp; Trust
for them to provide us a $225&nbsp;million senior unsecured revolving credit facility (the "Revolving Credit Facility"). Subject to the satisfactory completion of further syndication efforts, we
have the ability to increase the amount of the Revolving Credit Facility to an amount not exceeding $400&nbsp;million. We may use up to $50&nbsp;million of the Revolving Credit Facility for
letters of credit. Amounts available under the Revolving Credit Facility are subject to certain borrowing base limitations based upon, among other things, the amount of certain outstanding debt and
the amount of our eligible inventory, multiplied by advance rates determined by reference to the stage of development of each item of eligible inventory. At June&nbsp;30, 2001, our maximum limit for
borrowings and additional financial letters of credit was $176.3&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
may select an interest rate applicable to the borrowings under the Revolving Credit Facility based on either LIBOR, for a one, two, three or six-month term, or the
prime rate. Subject to our
then-effective leverage ratio, as defined, the interest rate may vary from LIBOR plus 1.75% to 2.50% or the prime rate plus 0% to 0.50%. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Revolving Credit Facility is guaranteed by certain of our wholly-owned subsidiaries. It has a three-year term, extendible to a full three-year term on each
anniversary of the closing date. Under the terms of the Revolving Credit Facility, we will be required to meet certain financial tests on an on-going basis, including minimum consolidated
tangible net worth, maximum ratio of consolidated liabilities to consolidated tangible net worth, minimum interest coverage, minimum liquidity and maximum inventory levels. Additionally, certain
covenants will limit our and our subsidiaries' ability to incur additional debt or guarantees, create, or permit to exist, liens on our property or grant negative pledges, make investments or
advances, merge with other entities, change the nature of our business, engage in transactions with affiliates and make asset sales. The Revolving Credit Facility also includes covenants restricting
dividends or prepayments of certain indebtedness, including the Notes. Under certain conditions, some of the terms of the Revolving Credit Facility, including pricing, may change. In addition, if
James K. Schuler ceases to be our CEO for any reason, his replacement must be approved by a majority of the lenders within 120&nbsp;days of his departure or removal in order to avoid an event of
default under the Revolving Credit Facility. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
obtained the Revolving Credit Facility to retire our former credit facilities and other outstanding indebtedness previously incurred by us or our subsidiaries and for general
corporate and working capital purposes. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
May&nbsp;1998, Schuler Residential issued $100&nbsp;million principal amount of 9% Senior Notes due April&nbsp;15, 2008. As a result of the merger of Schuler Residential into
us, these notes were assumed by us and guaranteed by the same subsidiaries guaranteeing the notes issued in the June&nbsp;2001 offerings. The 9% Senior Notes are senior unsecured obligations.
Interest on these notes is due and payable on April&nbsp;15 and October&nbsp;15 of each year. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
9% Senior Notes are not redeemable at our option prior to April&nbsp;15, 2003. Thereafter, these notes may be redeemed at a price initially equal to 104.50% of the principal
amount, decreasing in stages to 100% of the principal amount from and after April&nbsp;15, 2006, in each case together with accrued and unpaid interest. We will be obligated to make an offer to
purchase a portion of the 9% </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT SIZE=2>21</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<!-- ZEQ.=3,SEQ=21,EFW="2055720",CP="SCHULER HOMES, INC.",DN="1",CHK=866698,FOLIO='21',FILE='DISK012:[01MOC6.01MOC1746]FO1746A.;8',USER='CBABB',CD='14-AUG-2001;12:04' -->
<A NAME="page_fo1746_1_22"> </A>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>
Senior Notes if we do not maintain a minimum consolidated net worth, as defined, of at least $75&nbsp;million. We may also be required to offer to purchase these notes upon a change of control. In
addition, the 9% Senior Notes contain other restrictive covenants that, among other things, impose certain limitations on our liability to incur additional indebtedness, create liens, make restricted
payments, as defined, or sell assets. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
January&nbsp;1993, Schuler Residential issued $50&nbsp;million aggregate principal amount of 6.5% convertible subordinated debentures due January&nbsp;15, 2003. In
February&nbsp;1993, the related over-allotment option for an additional $7.5&nbsp;million was exercised in full. As a result of the merger of Schuler Residential into us, these
convertible subordinated debentures, were assumed by us. The convertible debentures are convertible at any time prior to maturity into shares of our common stock at a conversion price of $21.83 per
share, subject to certain adjustments. As of June&nbsp;30, 2001, none of the convertible debentures have been converted into shares of our common stock and the total principal amount outstanding was
$57.5&nbsp;million. During July&nbsp;2001, we repurchased $11.7&nbsp;million principal amount of our convertible subordinated debentures at a price equal to 100.75% of the principal amount. We
intend to redeem the remaining outstanding principal amount of these convertible debentures during our second quarter at a price equal to 101.0% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid
interest according to the terms and conditions of the convertible debentures. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
expect to acquire land for future homebuilding operations through takedowns of lots subject to option purchase contracts. The use of option contracts generally lessens
land-related risk and improves liquidity by allowing us to control a large number of lots with contract deposits. As of June&nbsp;30, 2001, we controlled approximately 28,500 lots in 79
communities. Of these lots, approximately 50% were under options contracts with deposits totaling $ 32.5&nbsp;million. We expect to utilize a combination of cash flow from operations and our
revolving credit facility to acquire these land parcels. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
have also entered into financial joint ventures to acquire and develop residential communities, typically with financial partners who fund the acquisition and development of land
and sell finished building sites to us pursuant to an option purchase contract and with sellers of land who contribute their property to the joint venture in exchange for a profits interest upon
completion and sale of the homes. As of June&nbsp;30, 2001, we were participating in 9 joint ventures totaling 1,077 building lots with an investment of $25.8&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During
the quarter ended June&nbsp;30, 2001, we incurred new debt secured by land purchased of approximately $8.9&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>


<P><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
have no material commitments or material off-balance sheet financing arrangements that would tend to affect future liquidity and anticipate that we can satisfy our
current and near-term capital requirements based on our current capital resources and additional liquidity available under our new credit facility. We believe we can meet our
long-term capital needs, including meeting debt payments and refinancing or paying off other long-term debt, from operations and external financing sources, assuming that no
significant adverse changes in our business or general economic conditions occur. However, we cannot assure you that we will not require additional financing and may need additional funds to support
more rapid expansion, respond to competitive pressures or respond to unanticipated requirements. We cannot assure you that additional funding will be available on attractive terms, or at all. </FONT></P>

Form of Promissory Note in connection with the Revolving Credit Agreement (included as Exhibit A to Exhibit 10.7).</FONT></TD>
